book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: Use Profiles for Location and Flow for Timing
body: Forthmann starts with recent auction context, uses profiles to narrow the relevant price area, then inspects executions for timing. Market profile and volume profile address time and volume acceptance respectively. The combined method asks what happens as the reference is reached.

book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: Main-Session Activity Shapes the Intraday Context
body: The book distinguishes participants by horizon and purpose, including hedgers, longer-horizon traders, and day traders. Their activity varies by instrument, release schedule, and primary session. Forthmann treats a single participant label as an interpretation of observed behavior.

book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: TPO Measures Time at Price
body: A market profile marks prices visited in successive time brackets, illustrated with half-hour letters. Wider rows show repeated visits across brackets. Its control price reflects the most TPO activity, which can differ from the price with the most executed volume.

book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: Initial Balance Anchors Opening Range Extension
body: The first opening brackets define an initial balance, often the first two half-hour brackets in the illustration. Trade beyond that range is an extension. Forthmann treats a relatively narrow balance as a reason to watch for expansion, and the active instrument and session matter.

book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: Single Prints Record a Brief Visit
body: A single-print price row belongs to just one TPO bracket. A single-column extension at a profile extreme is a buying or selling tail in the book's terminology. This locates brief acceptance or rejection to investigate on a revisit.

book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: Volume Point of Control Is a Price Mode
body: The VPOC is the price with the highest executed volume in the selected profile. Ordinary time-based volume shows how much traded in each time bar. A VPOC and time-based POC can therefore represent different prices in the same auction.

book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: A Naked POC Is Still Untested
body: Forthmann calls a prior control price that has not yet been revisited a naked POC. Price can later return to the level during a different auction. The actual reaction can be assessed with current profile and footprint context.

book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: Low-Volume Nodes Mark Thin Price Regions
body: Low-volume nodes are local indentations in a volume profile. They can appear between more accepted areas or along a fast directional move. Forthmann watches for either a reaction at a boundary or rapid passage through a thin region.

book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: Value Area Contains About Seventy Percent
body: Forthmann uses the approximately 70 percent of selected activity bracketed by value area high and value area low. The reference depends on the instrument, interval, and whether the distribution is volume or time based. It provides a way to compare the current open with prior acceptance.

book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: Track Acceptance Versus Reentry at Prior Value
body: The location of the open is only the first observation. Forthmann distinguishes an outside open that sustains activity beyond value from one that quickly returns inside. In balance, the prior control price can be an intermediate rotation reference.

book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: Treat Value-Area Traversal Rates as Historical Claims
body: The book mentions an older 80 percent rule for traversing prior value and qualifies its use in current markets. A reproducible test needs explicit definitions for the open, the entry back into value, target touch and observation horizon. A quoted historical heuristic is only a hypothesis for the repo.

book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: P and b Shapes Need Market Context
body: A P profile can show higher acceptance after a rally or a short-covering pause in a broader decline. A b shape can likewise appear in a down move or near a developing base. Forthmann looks at what came before and how the next auction behaves.

book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: Double Distributions Have Two Acceptance Regions
body: A double distribution occurs when the market spends time or trades heavily in one region, moves through a thinner transition, and builds a second concentration. It gives two potential reference zones and a transition area. The later open and subsequent activity help tell which zone matters.

book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: Compare Like Sessions Before Comparing Profiles
body: Fixed profiles provide consistent daily, weekly or monthly windows. Forthmann checks main-session and 24-hour profiles separately because they can place the highest-volume node at different prices. He emphasizes recent references and uses older levels selectively.

book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: Anchor a Flexible Profile to a Defined Auction
body: Flexible profiles can cover a specific trend, rotation, or multi-day range. The start and end must correspond to a recognizable event or trade window. Using the same range for TPO and volume makes differences in acceptance easier to interpret.

book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: Range Auction Can Show Two Control Prices
body: Forthmann profiles a defined range using both market and volume views. A TPO POC shows where time concentrated and VPOC shows where executions concentrated. Divergence identifies two reference prices to carry into the subsequent session.

book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: Developing POC Migration Tracks Moving Acceptance
body: When new trades build sufficient size at another price, the developing volume POC can migrate. Forthmann reads sustained migration in the context of an existing move and fresh initiative. He gives less weight to an isolated shift inside an established range.

book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: A Profile Bounce Can Start Before the Line
body: Forthmann treats strong volume and thin-profile transitions as zones. A retest may turn ahead of the original activity, react inside the band, or go through it. He uses the current response to distinguish these possibilities.

book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: Separate Accumulation From Short Follow-Up Pauses
body: Forthmann draws a flexible profile over an established rotation and watches order flow if a planned reference is nearby. He distinguishes this longer formation from a shorter pause after directional initiative has already appeared. The two pictures imply different stages of an auction.

book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: A Weak Extreme Can Advertise a Later Sweep
body: A weak high or low may consist of closely repeated prices with little decisive rejection. Forthmann treats that structure as a possible target for a later sweep. This chart-based usage of unfinished auction is distinct from a zero-quantity test inside a single footprint.

book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: DOM Displays Resting Depth at Each Price
body: The DOM shows current resting limit orders around the market. Aggressive trades can consume liquidity at the best bid or ask, but resting quotes can change or disappear. Forthmann uses executed flow and price response alongside displayed depth.

book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: Tape Speed Is an Alert to Read Context
body: The book uses large-print and speed-of-tape displays to call attention to an acceleration near a swing, reference zone, or stop run. The display alerts the trader to inspect the next price reaction. A burst can mark exhaustion or the start of a directional move.

book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: Footprints Time a Move at a Known Level
body: A footprint decomposes each bar into executed volume per price level and side. Forthmann looks for the sequence of imbalances around a mapped reference. His examples allow the chain to contain a break and use an illustrative ratio distinct from Dale's software default.

book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: Stack Settings Depend on Platform and Instrument
body: The E-mini illustration compares adjacent price rows and illustrates a two-to-one labeling example. Forthmann also allows interpretation of an imperfect stack when neighboring activity supports it. A runnable test needs to declare the ratio, adjacency, minimum size, and treatment of gaps.

book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: Confirm a Footprint Impulse With Price Progress
body: Forthmann checks whether price and successive local control prices advance after a first stack or large execution. If an opposing print cannot move price through an extreme, the next impulse can clarify which side is gaining initiative. A preidentified reference gives the sequence context.

book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: Absorption Appears as Execution Without Progress
body: Strong buy-initiated executions can hit passive selling while price fails to establish a new high. The mirrored case has heavy selling with a defended low. Forthmann compares price and delta to infer this condition, with replenishing liquidity as one explanation.

book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: Icebergs Are an Inference From Repeated Fills
body: Hidden or replenishing liquidity can produce many executions at one level without sustained movement. Displayed DOM depth alone cannot reveal total hidden interest or the owner. The useful observation is persistent execution with a disproportionate or absent price response.

book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: Wait for Narrow Opening Balance to Resolve
body: In the Hang Seng example, a narrow range forms near the active open while delta keeps falling and price holds a higher low. The later upward VPOC crossing helps confirm resolution. The example separates the initial stall from the later directional evidence.

book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: Price Sometimes Moves Before Delta Catches Up
body: Forthmann shows both the standard absorption divergence and another sequence in which price has already turned while delta still lags. Compare synchronized panels, observe the next footprint imbalance, and note when the disagreement resolves. The ordering matters for any replay study.

book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: Delta Has Time and Volume-at-Price Views
body: The book shows signed delta by bar, CVD and delta distributed across price levels. The views can locate stretches of related aggression or a large apparent buying or selling extreme. Comparing those prints with actual price progress is part of interpreting them.

book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: Prepare Active-Session References Before the Opening
body: Forthmann reviews the prior main-session high and low, overnight or early-session extrema, recent value and POCs, and the scheduled release calendar. Preparation creates scenarios for the open. The source's timing examples should be interpreted for their specific instrument and session.

book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: Volatility Needs Adequate Liquidity to Be Useful
body: The book separates tradable expansion from volatile action with thin liquidity and poor follow-through. Its examples show long wicks, overlapping bars, and erratic swings in the latter case. Instrument and session selection matter alongside measured range.

book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: Footprint Magnitudes Depend on the Instrument
body: In choosing markets, Forthmann compares pace, session timing, liquidity and usual contract sizes. A large print in a thin contract can look small in a more active contract. Use comparable session windows before interpreting relative activity.

book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: An Opening Drive Depends on the Prior Auction
body: Forthmann distinguishes directional opening initiative from a test or rotation. An early push following consolidation can carry a different meaning from a push after several already extended sessions. Earlier tails, value and the new auction provide reference points.

book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: Use Profile Tails to Frame False Breaks
body: The crude and E-mini examples establish a short opening range, show a break that fails, then use lower-timeframe footprints to assess the response. Existing single-print tails and value structure give the probe a defined location. A subsequent stack is interpreted in the context of that sequence.

book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: A Hanging Ledge Can Be a Continuation Pause
body: A ledge is a compact pause inside a larger move. Forthmann profiles the ledge, examines its developing control price, and uses follow-through to distinguish continuation from an attempted reversal. A P shape can form during temporary short covering in a downtrend.

book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: Broadening Swings Need a Confirmed Failure
body: The book's broadening-top example marks expanding highs and lows and waits for a completed structural failure. The larger shape serves as warning context, with the subsequent failed move providing more concrete evidence. Flexible profiles map reference areas around it.

book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: Work From Higher-Timeframe Location to Footprint
body: The yen and E-mini studies first locate price around an established profile or recent extreme. A smaller price/delta view then shows whether aggression gains progress, and the footprint checks for a later initiative print or imbalance. The final entry assessment follows that order.

book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: Examples Combine Distinct Pieces of Auction Evidence
body: FDAX uses a previous VPOC with local delta and footprint evidence, Bund uses a double distribution and later buying sequence, and crude profiles successive intraday legs. Each case applies the same sequence to different market speeds. The examples illustrate the author's process on selected trades.

book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: Weekly Profiles Can Supply Local Reference Levels
body: Forthmann projects a weekly VPOC onto a faster crude chart to observe the next interaction. The gold and EUR/USD examples similarly use earlier structure before zooming into delta and footprints. The higher-timeframe reference and lower-timeframe trigger are separate inputs.

book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: Evaluate a False Break by Its Return
body: Forthmann describes popular breakouts and reversal formations that fail, leaving traders positioned in the wrong direction. Confirmation comes from rejection, reentry, and a subsequent attempt in the opposite direction. The recognizable formation helps define where a test occurred.

book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: Track Prior and Overnight Extremes for Sweeps
body: The book shows squeezes and prior-day or non-institutional highs and lows getting taken during the main session. The useful observation is how price responds after the extreme is reached, with profile and order flow supplying context. A sweep by itself only identifies the path through the level.

book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: Treat a Trend as Swing Progression
body: Forthmann discusses preceding swing highs and lows, closes beyond them, and follow-up behavior to read a trend. A local visual pattern can look different across chart intervals. Sustained progress and a defended retest give the structure more context.

book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: Tie Invalidation to Failed Price Progress
body: The book uses structure and thinner profile zones in location and risk decisions. Failure to make expected swing progress can call the trade premise into question. Forthmann emphasizes timely exits and prepares the trade plan before the decision point.

book_title: Volume Profile, Market Profile, Order Flow: Next Generation of Daytrading
author: Johannes Forthmann
file_path: books/Volume Profile & Market Profile Order Flow for Next Gen Daytrading.pdf
title: Separate Initial Setup From Multi-Session Holding
body: The final EUR/USD example begins with a local backfire setup and then shows the wider hourly path over subsequent sessions. The original evidence and the later holding decision have different horizons. It is an example of how the method scales across views.
